keyFindings.description: The stall branch (main.go:459-475) returns 200 degraded before the durable-consumer checks (main.go:487-499), so while a stall is past bus.RepairGrace a durable that is gone (ErrConsumerNotFound), unanswered within healthzBudget, or not bound to this listener's subscription answers 200 degraded naming the wrong fault, where it answered 503 before. Such a listener receives nothing, so the reason for 200 (stale caches still place fanout messages) does not hold. The deep review's probe test shows it: recreated durable plus a failing hook gives 503 under the grace and 200 degraded after clock.Advance(bus.RepairGrace). Move the stall check after the durable checks, just before the healthy answer, and add that case to healthz_hook_stall_test.go.

kvwatch.go:223, :744-745 and packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:2538 cite cmd/listener/main.go:123 and main.go:177; at this head those are envDuration and a doc-comment line (the numbers were the reviewer's own in round 1 and moved with the merges). hook_stall_test.go:68 says the stall is exposed 'so cmd/listener can answer 503 on /healthz', and :96 says the error is 'no reason for /healthz to refuse'; the answer is 200 degraded.

HookStall's doc (nats.go:570-572) says a run that succeeds clears the error 'in the same locked section that zeroes the stall'; a successful run during which another event landed clears the error but restarts the stall (recovery.go, rewatch's else branch), which is the case main.go:467-472 handles.
recovery.go:250-251 says the two messages and the three attributes are matched by the AWS log-metric filter; the filter (metricfilters.go:103) matches only the ERROR message's words and the level.

The census's own healthz search hits four listener health checks it does not list: packages/envoy/deploy/compose/listener.compose.yml:15 and single-node.compose.yml:43 (curl -f), packages/envoy/infra/host/listener.go:248 (Docker health check) and infra/host/watchdog.go:38 (curl -sf). All pass on 200, so each is 'unchanged', but each needs its row.

The fragment does not name the log contract change an operator's filter reads: the ERROR 'envoy nats reconnect hook failed' is now the WARN 'envoy nats reconnect hook failed; it is retried' under a minute and the ERROR 'envoy nats reconnect hooks have not succeeded' past it, with a new stall_ms attribute, and kvwatch's reason 'repair failed' is gone.
